source.regression:
ONE

naming TWO streams. mapBinTypes used to gate the black-bin (refuse) rule behind `streams.length === 0`, so 'Black bin and food caddy' matched food, the gate was skipped, and the refuse collection vanished. The pre-per-council code returned ['general','food']; the gated version returned ['food'] only. Membership is the fix; the order is now restored to the pre-fix ['general','food'] because the unambiguous colours are pushed above the stream-word block.

source.regression: Green was gated behind `streams.length === 0`, so the food caddy match on this line skipped the gate and the garden half was lost: 'Green bin and food caddy' returned ['food'] only. Under-detecting garden costs a user a real collection, which is worse than the reverse error, so green is no longer gated. Green is unambiguous for NED (refuse Black / recycling Burgundy / garden Green / food Brown) and is never recycling. Order is ['garden','food'] so the day's summary reads 'Green and food bins'.

source.note: Synthetic minimal input shaped to the parser contract: one NEGATED line that carries a real date, plus one real collection so a phantom would be visible in the stream list rather than hidden by an empty result. NOT a live recording. Replace with a real recording from https://www.ne-derbyshire.gov.uk/bins-and-recycling/bin-collection-dates when network access is available.
source.regression: The two-word guard /no (collection|recycling)/ did not match the container-qualified 'No green bin collection', so the line produced a phantom ['garden'] collection on a date where no garden bin was due. This was reachable BEFORE the green gate was removed as well -- the old code also returned ['garden'] here -- so it is a pre-existing bug, not one introduced by ungating green. NO_COLLECTION_RE now allows intervening adjectives. A real Black bin line sits alongside it so the negation is what decides the stream list.
